facts.text: Leonhard Schaetz 在诺华（Novartis）放射配体治疗（RLT）运营团队担任 International Head Health System Readiness & Partnership Radioligand Therapy（RLT）,即国际医疗卫生体系准备与合作伙伴关系负责人。
其所在的诺华 Radioligand Therapy Operations 部门聚焦放射配体治疗产品的管理、战略与运营及合作伙伴关系,团队还包括国际医学事务、供应链、临床供应管理等方向的负责人。

他是 2026 年发表于 The Lancet Regional Health – Europe(Elsevier)的研究《Estimation of future patient populations eligible for radioligand therapies in the EU and the UK: a modelling study》的作者之一;该研究估算欧盟及英国未来可接受放射配体治疗的患者规模,并评估医疗体系容量压力。
该研究由欧洲委员会联合研究中心（JRC）与 WifOR 合作完成,其中 WifOR 部分由诺华制药（Novartis Pharma AG）资助;研究估计 2025–2035 年间 EU-27 理论上符合条件的 RLT 患者池可能从约 1.1万–1.3万 增至约 13万–18万。

background.text: Leonhard Schaetz 是诺华放射配体治疗（RLT）运营团队的国际医疗卫生体系准备与合作伙伴关系负责人（International Head Health System Readiness & Partnership RLT）。这不是一个临床医生职位,而是企业运营与体系协作岗位:他的工作方向是帮助各国医疗卫生体系为放射配体治疗的可及性、容量和落地做好准备,并与外部伙伴建立合作。其所在团队涵盖国际医学事务、供应链、临床供应管理、患者路径与合作伙伴关系等职能。

与其岗位主题相符,他是 2026 年 JRC 与 WifOR 合作发表在 The Lancet Regional Health – Europe 的建模研究作者之一,该研究估算了 EU-27、EU-4 及英国未来十年符合 RLT 条件的患者池规模,并指出 RLT 的预期增长可能使现有治疗容量(即便在核医学基础设施较完善的国家)面临压力,需要各国协同努力以保障患者可及并减少肿瘤诊疗中的健康不平等。该研究由诺华资助(WifOR 部分)。

qa.question: 他的具体职位和职能是什么?
qa.answer: 他是诺华 Radioligand Therapy Operations 团队的 International Head Health System Readiness & Partnership RLT,即国际层面的医疗卫生体系准备与合作伙伴关系负责人,属于企业运营/体系协作角色,而非临床医生。

qa.question: 与他工作最相关的研究成果是什么?
qa.answer: 他参与撰写了 2026 年 The Lancet Regional Health – Europe 的研究《Estimation of future patient populations eligible for radioligand therapies in the EU and the UK: a modelling study》,内容为欧盟及英国 RLT 适用患者规模与医疗体系容量的建模估算。

qa.question: 交流时哪些议题与他的职责最贴近?
qa.answer: 医疗卫生体系对 RLT 的准备度(核医学基础设施、治疗容量)、国际层面的患者可及性与伙伴合作模式等议题与其职务描述及合作研究的主题直接相关;具体在谈的工作重点和当前计划最好与他本人确认。

qa.question: 他所在团队还有哪些职能方向?
qa.answer: 该团队还包括国际前列腺癌方向总监、区域医学总监、国际医学事务总监、RLT 平台全球供应链负责人、临床供应管理、患者路径与合作伙伴关系等职能,反映 RLT 从医学事务到供应链运营的完整链条。

qa.question: 他参与的研究有哪些资助背景?
qa.answer: 其参与的 JRC/WifOR 建模研究中,WifOR 部分由 Novartis Pharma AG 资助,JRC 部分由欧盟委员会研究框架计划预算支持;在引用或讨论该研究结论时应留意这一资助关系。

Estimation of future patient populations eligible for radioligand therapies in the EU and the UK: a modelling study
Background
The eligible patient population for radioligand therapies (RLTs) has the potential to grow rapidly in the coming years. European healthcare systems may be ill-prepared to provide the additional treatment capacity required on top of current workload. To address this challenge, data on the size of the eligible patient pool and the potential utilisation of RLTs are needed.
Methods
The maximum pool of patients theoretically eligible for RLTs over the next decade was estimated for the 27 EU member states (EU-27) using incidence data, and additionally for France, Germany, Italy, Spain (EU-4) and the UK using prevalence data. Conditions for which RLT are currently authorised, potential expansions of existing authorisations to earlier disease stages, and anticipated authorisations for products in development were analysed.
Findings
Between 2025 and 2035 in the EU-27, the patient pool theoretically eligible for RLTs could increase from 11,000 to 13,000 to approximately 130,000–180,000. A scenario based on preliminary utilisation data suggests that, in the EU-4, 17,000–35,000 patients from this pool could be treated in 2030, increasing to approximately 37,000 patients by 2035.
Interpretation
The expected uptake of RLTs in EU healthcare systems over the coming decade may overwhelm available treatment capacity, even in countries with well-developed nuclear medicine infrastructure. Efforts across all EU countries will be required to ensure adequate patient access to RLTs and to minimise health inequalities in cancer care.
Funding
Research by WifOR was funded by Novartis Pharma AG. JRC research was covered by the European Commission’s Research Framework Programmes budget.

Estimation of future patient populations eligible for radioligand therapies in the EU and the UK: a modelling study
Background
The eligible patient population for radioligand therapies (RLTs) has the potential to grow rapidly in the coming years. European healthcare systems may be ill-prepared to provide the additional treatment capacity required on top of current workload. To address this challenge, data on the size of the eligible patient pool and the potential utilisation of RLTs are needed.
